R101.note: mongoose.sanitizeFilter() wraps $-prefixed nested objects in $eq before findOne, closing the operator-injection bypass of ownerId/_id as the case's own comment prescribes; scalar extraCriteria still passes through unchanged.

R102.note: path.basename(pluginName) strips directory components before the require() concatenation, closing traversal; loadedPlugins cache is still keyed by the raw name but that is harmless.

R103.note: Only switches HttpGet to HttpPost; no [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] or equivalent token check is added, and the write-up's claim that browsers block cross-origin form POST submissions is factually wrong (that is exactly how classic CSRF works), so an auto-submitting cross-site form likely still triggers the delete.

R104.note: Reverts to JNDI's parameterized filter ({0}/{1} placeholders with filterArgs), which JNDI escapes server-side; preserves original query logic and output handling.

R105.note: Adds a length check before strcpy/strcat and returns -1 on oversized input instead of truncating, matching the stated contract exactly; valid-input path unchanged.

R106.note: Standard mysqli prepared statement with bound parameter; return contract (null on failure, array on success) preserved.

R107.note: Whitelist validation in the service layer preserves #{tenantId} binding and the created_at default; rejecting non-whitelisted sort values is explicitly required by the stated contract, so the added restriction is not a penalized regression.

R108.note: Stored extension now derived from file-type's content-based detection instead of the client-supplied originalname; detection already gates on ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES so legitimate uploads are unaffected.

R109.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES, UTF-8) applied at the point of HTML concatenation for both fields; standard, correct output encoding.

R110.note: Bounds check on channelIndex before the array write, consistent with the function's existing early-return style; valid updates unaffected.

R111.note: smtplib.sendmail() replaces raw docmd() envelope construction and Python's putcmd() rejects CR/LF since the cited patch versions, closing the injection; but it silently drops the explicit EHLO hostname ('bounce-notifier.example.com') in favor of smtplib's auto-detected local hostname, an unstated protocol-level behavior change.

R112.note: WHERE id = ANY($1) with the ids array bound as a single parameter is the standard safe pg pattern for this case; matches the stated contract, including graceful handling of an empty ids array.

R113.note: pathinfo(..., PATHINFO_EXTENSION) checks only the final extension, closing the double-extension bypass; legitimate single-extension filenames unaffected.

R114.note: resize(count) fixes the out-of-bounds write into packet, but the loop still reads fields[i] unbounded, so a count larger than fields.size() still produces an out-of-bounds read - the stated contract explicitly required rejecting/reporting that case, and this fix does not implement it.

R115.note: Self-injects a @Lazy proxy and routes the loop's call through self.deleteInvoice(), the standard fix for Spring AOP self-invocation bypassing @PreAuthorize; no other behavior change.

R116.note: Replaces the string-built setTimeout argument with a closure callback capturing reminderId/message as values, the idiomatic fix; recordReminder is invoked identically to before.
